Labor market figures reinforced signs of cooling: Brazil generated 121,305 formal jobs in September, well below market forecasts of 171,000. title: Indonesian Shares Set for Second weekly Decline
body: Indonesia's IDX Composite sank 91 points, or 1.8%, to 4,939 in Friday morning trade, erasing gains from the previous two sessions after a tech-led selloff on Wall Street overnight, driven by renewed doubts over the profitability of massive AI investments following the U.S. midterm elections. title: Australia 10Y Yield Holds Near August Low
body: Australia's 10-year government bond yield hovered around 5.0%, near its lowest level since late August, as global bond markets rallied on rising safe-haven demand following a sharp selloff in technology stocks. Investor anxiety deepened after the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections stoked concerns that tighter regulation could slow AI investment, triggering a rally in US Treasuries that flowed through to Australian bonds. The move lower in yields was further supported by the Reserve Bank of Australia's 3 November decision. Although the RBA lifted the cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85%, the hike was passed on a narrowly split 6–3 vote and was accompanied by less hawkish guidance, reinforcing expectations that policy rates have likely peaked. Still, Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser cautioned that a loss of confidence in the RBA could make inflation more difficult and costly to control, potentially forcing a more forceful policy response. Interest-rate swaps now imply only about a 6% probability of another rate increase in December, while a 25-basis-point cut is fully priced in by year-end. With this performance, total tourist arrivals for the first ten months of 2026 reached 1,862,304. India remained Sri Lanka's largest source market, contributing 62,211 visitors, or 37% of total arrivals for the month. The United Kingdom followed with 12,402 visitors, China with 11,190, Australia with 8,509 and Germany with 8,027. Average daily arrivals in October stood at around 5,440, with a peak of 7,045 recorded on 17 October. The week of 15–21 October saw the highest weekly inflow, with 42,739 arrivals. The October upturn came after a 0.3% year-on-year decline in arrivals in September. Cumulative arrivals up to the end of September were still 1.8% lower than a year earlier. In parallel, tourism earnings in September rose 1.5% year-on-year to $186 million, although total tourism revenue for January–September fell 9.2% to $2.2 billion. title: South Korean Shares Sinks Below 5,000
body: The benchmark KOSPI plunged 7.77% to around 4,966 on Friday, sliding below the 5,000 mark to a nine-month low as a steep sell-off in technology stocks followed an overnight rout on Wall Street. Investor anxiety deepened after the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections fueled fears that tighter regulations could slow investment in AI infrastructure and data centers. The tech-heavy Nasdaq tumbled 5.52%, while the S&P 500 fell 4.36%. South Korean chipmakers were hit hardest, with Samsung Electronics sinking 7.99% and SK Hynix tumbling 9.97%. The sharp drop triggered a circuit breaker shortly after the opening bell, halting KOSPI trading for 20 minutes from 9:03 a.m. In addition, rising oil prices amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz further weighed on sentiment. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il vowed to introduce measures to stabilize markets, while the trading suspension marked the 10th circuit breaker activation this year. title: Philippines Jobless Rate Ticks Up to 5.4%
body: The unemployment rate in the Philippines edged up to 5.4% in September 2026 from 5.3% in August. The number of unemployed individuals increased to 2.86 million from 2.77 million, while the employment rate eased slightly to 94.6% from 94.7%. Despite this, the number of employed persons grew to 50.32 million from 49.79 million over the same period. The underemployment rate declined to 11.0% from 11.9%, with 5.56 million workers looking for additional hours of work or an additional job. On a year-on-year basis, the unemployment rate in September 2026 was higher than the 3.8% recorded in September 2025. The employment rate was also lower than the 96.2% posted a year earlier, although the number of employed persons rose from 49.60 million in September 2025. The underemployment rate, at 11.0%, was slightly down from 11.1% a year earlier. By sector, services remained the largest source of employment, accounting for 62.2% of total jobs, followed by agriculture at 20.7% and industry at 17.1%. Average weekly working hours increased to 40.1 in September 2026 from 39.2 in August, but were lower than the 40.5 hours recorded a year earlier. title: Philippines Manufacturing Output Rises 12.7% in September
body: Manufacturing production in the Philippines expanded by 12.7% year-on-year in September 2026, accelerating from a downwardly revised 10% increase in August and marking the fastest growth since June. The upturn was driven largely by a surge in the manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products (39.6% vs 25% in August), which contributed 34.2% to the overall acceleration. Significant support also came from basic metals (37.1% vs 24.6%), transport equipment (16.1% vs 9.1%), and rubber and plastic products (18% vs 13.8%). By contrast, growth in the manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products eased to 23.4% from 30.7%. Food production declined by 2.9%, reversing a 0.3% increase in the previous month, amid a slowdown in six of the eight food-related industry groups. The downturn was led by the manufacture of prepared animal feeds, where growth decelerated to 5.8% from 17.9%. Over the January–September period, overall manufacturing output was 9.3% higher than in the same period a year earlier. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Gold Heads for Strong Weekly Gain
body: Gold climbed toward $4,100 per ounce on Friday and was poised to gain more than 5% for the week, following a sweeping Democratic victory in the US midterm elections. Markets now expect Democrats to press for an end to the Iran conflict, a development that could push oil prices lower, ease inflationary pressures, and reduce the likelihood of more aggressive interest rate hikes. Investors also anticipate that a divided government may constrain President Donald Trump's fiscal agenda, limiting additional government spending and borrowing and further tempering inflation concerns. At the same time, the global equity selloff intensified amid fears that Democrats could introduce stricter regulations on the artificial intelligence industry and slow data center expansion, triggering some liquidity-driven selling in precious metals. Even so, these headwinds were counterbalanced by stronger demand for safe-haven bonds, which pushed yields lower and bolstered appetite for non-yielding assets such as gold. title: Nikkei Extends Losses as AI Selloff Intensifies

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slid into correction territory as mounting pressure on artificial intelligence shares sparked a broad selloff. The downturn intensified after a sweeping Democratic victory in the US midterm elections fueled concerns over stricter regulation of the AI industry and a potential slowdown in data center expansion. title: US Futures Extend Declines After AI Rout
body: US stock futures extended their decline on Friday after the major averages posted their worst single-day drop since the tariff-driven market turmoil of April 2025, amid mounting concerns that Democrats could introduce tighter regulations on the artificial intelligence sector. Futures linked to the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq 100 were all down at least 0.5%. In Thursday's regular session, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite sank 5.5%, while the Dow and S&P 500 fell 3.4% and 4.4%, respectively. All 11 S&P 500 sectors finished in the red, with companies tied to AI infrastructure suffering the largest losses. Investor sentiment deteriorated on fears that Democratic policy initiatives could slow the pace of data center expansion. Chipmakers and memory-related stocks were among the hardest hit, including Nvidia (-9.3%), AMD (-17.3%), Micron (-17.5%), and SanDisk (-22.3%). title: Oil Set for Sharp Weekly Decline
body: Crude oil hovered around $91 per barrel on Friday and was on track for a weekly loss of roughly 12%. The decline was largely attributed to optimism that the Middle East conflict might be resolved more quickly, following a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections, even as significant uncertainties remain. With Democrats securing control of both houses of Congress, President Donald Trump's ability to sustain strong support for military action against Iran could be constrained. Tehran is reportedly reviewing proposals submitted by mediators on its nuclear program, but has reiterated that it will require the lifting of the US naval blockade on its ports, an easing of sanctions and the release of frozen assets before it fully reopens the Strait of Hormuz. At the same time, at least five vessel-related incidents have been reported in the Persian Gulf since Sunday, underscoring ongoing risks to maritime shipping. Nevertheless, conditions have improved markedly. Crude exports from the Gulf have rebounded to near pre-war levels, although transportation and insurance costs remain elevated.
